hero.title: Mermaid live editor,
hero.titleAccent: visual and code in one place
hero.description: Most mermaid editors give you a text box and a preview. This one also gives you a canvas: click to add a block, drag an arrow, group things into areas — and the mermaid code writes itself. Switch to the code tab and edit it by hand; the canvas follows.

statCards.title: Renders as you type
statCards.sub: The real mermaid engine, redrawn a few hundred milliseconds after your last keystroke.

statCards.title: Code and canvas sync
statCards.sub: Edit either side. The other one catches up — no copy-paste between two tools.

statCards.title: 14 node shapes
statCards.sub: Rectangle, rounded, pill, circle, diamond, database, hexagon and the rest, one click each.

statCards.title: Free, email only
statCards.sub: No trial, no export watermark — your email is all you need to save your diagrams.

spotlights.heading: A canvas, not just a text box
spotlights.sub: The visual tab is a real editor on top of the rendered diagram: click a node to select it, double-click to rename it in place, drag anywhere to pan.

bullets.title: Click to build
bullets.sub: Add a block, point an arrow at another one, label the arrow. No syntax to remember before you start.

bullets.title: Pick a shape
bullets.sub: Fourteen mermaid flowchart shapes — decision diamonds, database cylinders, subroutines — from one picker.

bullets.title: Colour anything
bullets.sub: Eight presets plus a colour picker, applied to a single node or to a whole area.

spotlights.heading: Mermaid code that stays yours
spotlights.sub: The text tab is plain mermaid — the same syntax GitHub, GitLab, Notion and Obsidian already render. Nothing here is a proprietary format.

bullets.title: Write it by hand
bullets.sub: Type mermaid directly and watch it render. Six ready-made examples to start from.

bullets.title: Round-trips
bullets.sub: Flowcharts you paste in are parsed back onto the canvas — nodes, shapes, colours, subgraphs and all.

bullets.title: Every diagram type
bullets.sub: Flowchart, sequence, class, state, ER, gantt, git graph, pie — the preview renders whatever mermaid supports.

spotlights.heading: Big diagrams stay readable
spotlights.sub: Architecture diagrams outgrow one screen fast. Pan, zoom and grouping are built for that instead of fighting it.

bullets.title: Areas and nesting
bullets.sub: Group blocks into subgraphs, nest an area inside another, move a whole subtree in one gesture.

bullets.title: Zoom from 2% to 1600%
bullets.sub: Scroll to pan, ctrl-scroll to zoom, or re-centre with one button.

bullets.title: Saved as you go
bullets.sub: Your diagram autosaves to your account as you edit — close the tab and pick it up on any device.

spotlights.heading: Export and get on with it
spotlights.sub: Nothing is locked in. Take the picture, take the source, or take a Markdown block ready to paste into a document.

bullets.title: No paywall
bullets.sub: Every feature, including export, is free. There is no paid tier to upgrade to.

bullets.title: Rendered in your browser
bullets.sub: Rendering happens in your browser; saved diagrams live in your account, so they're there on any device.

bullets.title: SVG, PNG, .mmd, .md
bullets.sub: Copy the SVG markup, download a 2x PNG, save the mermaid source, or grab a fenced Markdown block.

comparison.title: How it compares to
comparison.description: Diagram-as-code tools make you write everything by hand. Drag-and-drop tools give you a picture you cannot diff. This one refuses to pick a side.

rows.title: Getting started
rows.us: Double-click the canvas and a node appears. You can learn the syntax later, or never.
rows.them: Read the syntax reference first, or accept a drawing tool with no text representation at all.

rows.title: The output format
rows.us: Plain mermaid — the same text GitHub, GitLab and Notion render natively.
rows.them: A proprietary file that only opens in the tool that made it.

rows.title: Editing later
rows.us: Change the code or move the blocks. Both directions work on the same diagram.
rows.them: One direction only: code-first tools have no canvas, canvas-first tools have no source.

rows.title: Price
rows.them: Free tier capped at a few diagrams, with export or collaboration behind a subscription.

rows.title: Where the data lives
rows.us: In your account — an email to sign in, and your diagrams follow you to any device.
rows.them: An account on someone's server, with your diagrams attached to it.

faq.heading: Mermaid editor
faq.sub: All you need to start is an email.

items.a: Mermaid is a text syntax for diagrams: you describe nodes and arrows in a few lines, and a renderer draws the picture. GitHub, GitLab, Notion and Obsidian render it inside Markdown, so a mermaid block stays readable in a pull request or a wiki page.

items.q: Is this mermaid editor really free?
items.a: Yes. Every feature, including SVG and PNG export, is free. All you need is an email to sign in — there is no paid tier and nothing is held back.

items.q: Do I need to know mermaid syntax?
items.a: No. Start on the visual tab: double-click the canvas to add a block, select it and draw an arrow to another one. The mermaid code is generated for you and you can read it whenever you want to learn the syntax.

The code tab renders anything mermaid supports — flowchart, sequence, class, state, entity relationship, gantt, git graph, pie and more. The visual canvas edits flowcharts specifically, which is what most diagrams are.

items.q: Can I export to PNG or SVG?
items.a: Yes. Copy the SVG markup to the clipboard, download the SVG file, or download a PNG rendered at 2x for slides and documents. You can also save the mermaid source as .mmd or as a fenced Markdown block.
Your diagrams are saved to your account, so they are there whenever you come back — on any device. Export the source if you ever want a local copy.

items.q: Can I paste in an existing mermaid diagram?
items.a: Yes. Paste it into the code tab; a flowchart is parsed back onto the visual canvas with its nodes, shapes, colours and subgraphs intact. Other diagram types render in the preview but stay code-only.
Rendering happens entirely in your browser, so once the page has loaded the editor keeps working without a connection.

finalCta.heading: Open the editor.
finalCta.sub: A blank canvas, a code tab and every export option — free, in your browser, right now.
